sections.title: What are Large Language Models?
sections.body: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are advanced computer systems that understand and generate human language. They are built using a type of artificial intelligence called neural networks, which learn from vast amounts of text data. This training helps them predict what words or phrases should come next in a sentence.

sections.title: How LLMs Process Text
sections.body: LLMs break down text into smaller pieces called tokens, which can be words, subwords, or even characters. These tokens are transformed into numerical representations, known as embeddings, that capture the meaning and relationships between words. This process allows LLMs to understand context and generate relevant responses.

sections.title: The Role of Prompts
sections.body: Prompts are the questions or statements we give to LLMs to guide their responses. The way we phrase these prompts can greatly influence the quality of the answers we receive. By carefully designing prompts, we can improve the relevance and accuracy of the LLM's output.

sections.title: Enhancing LLM Performance
sections.body: Techniques like prompt engineering and automatic prompt generation help customize how LLMs respond. For example, Chain-of-Thought prompting encourages the model to explain its reasoning step-by-step, which can lead to more accurate answers. These methods are especially useful in educational settings where clear and reliable information is crucial.
